On Android 12 and later, the caller number is only delivered to apps that hold call log permission; without it, only a generic "incoming call" is spoken and the caller name is never announced even if saved in your contacts. This app is made for blind and low-vision users: granting the log lets it announce the caller by voice before answering, so a blind user knows who is calling before lifting the phone. The permission is used for announcing the name only; nothing else is read.

Some manufacturers pause background voice announcements to save battery. Grant Nateq an exemption from battery optimization and open the app settings to confirm background announcements keep working.
Xiaomi/Redmi/POCO device: Nateq needs a battery optimization exemption and "Autostart" enabled under Mi security management to keep background voice announcements alive.
Huawei/Honor device: enable the battery exemption and "Auto-launch" under System Manager (Apps > Special) so background voice announcements keep working.
Oppo/OnePlus/realme device: open the battery exemption and allow Nateq under "Startup management" in the security center to keep background announcements alive.
Vivo device: enable the battery exemption and "Auto start" under the permission manager so background voice announcements keep working.
Samsung device: enable the battery exemption, open the app settings, and keep Nateq out of "Sleeping apps" so background voice announcements keep working.

Uses the system exact alarm (setAlarmClock) to bypass all Doze and battery limits, so the time announcement fires at the exact minute; the side effect is a persistent alarm icon in the status bar.

Version %1$s
• Error and diagnostic log sharing with developer: integrated dialog to collect app logs, engine states, and device diagnostics to share as a file or via Telegram support bot with bot support for log files and voice messages, and case-insensitive pronunciation for data storage units (MB, GB, TB)
• Fixed time period pronunciation to "مساءاً" across time announcements and text conversion to prevent pausal silencing on modern Android 17 TTS engines
• Independent number reading language setting (always Arabic or English without exception): all numeric segments are attributed immediately and exclusively to the selected language across screen reading, announcements, and text processing pipelines
• Removed automatic engine selection and runtime fallback: the app strictly adheres to the user-selected engine and voice per language, displaying engine configuration status clearly in settings with instant audible failure alerts
• Permanent per-engine RMS calibration & codebase line normalization: stable, saved loudness gain for each engine prevents volume pumping, and clean line endings across the repository
• Text-processor prewarm: the first spoken announcement after launch starts instantly with no initial freeze
• Franco-Arabic understanding: words like "3ashan" and "7abibi" are spoken as proper Arabic instead of English spelling
• Simple in-text SSML support: <break> pauses, <say-as> spelling, and encoded entities are translated into natural speech
• Per-language pronunciation dictionary: language-specific entries merge over the shared dictionary when speaking that language, specific wins
• ProGuard cleanup and project line-ending normalization
• Instant speech preview across every audio section (time announcement & the hourly chime, notifications, SMS, caller, battery): the "listen" button speaks the sample with the currently displayed values straight from the screen — no saving needed — and a screen-reader announcement marks its start and end
• The exact-alarm permission row now explains the situation and opens the "manufacturer guidance" section with one tap
• A new "max precision" option for time announcements: schedules a real alarm-clock alarm (setAlarmClock) with its status-bar alarm icon for the strongest Doze wake-up guarantee — re-schedules immediately when enabled
• Import fix for the time announcement interval: step-5 values (10/55…) restore correctly instead of snapping to 30
• System TTS settings no longer crash when choosing the default engine (Samsung): voice names for third languages carried a lang-local suffix, which is not a valid locale, so the system text-to-speech screen crashed — names are now proper locale forms (fr/de/es) so selecting the engine works without stopping, and already stored old values upgrade automatically
• Update detection fixed after the asset rename: the app no longer reports "up to date" when it cannot find the APK asset under its expected name — it picks any published .apk asset (preferring the current name), so the update shows as available; this fix is also published on GitHub with a legacy-named alias asset so older installed builds can reach it
• A selectable second language for text conversion: a short foreign word not detected inside Arabic text is now spoken in a language of your choice (French/German/Spanish…) instead of the default English, with ready sample voices in the "sample text" screen
• Arabic diacritics are now kept automatically with engines that understand them (such as Google TTS) without requiring the switch, and stay fully optional with other engines
• Engine language is checked before speaking: if a voice engine lacks the text language, the app falls back to a capable engine immediately instead of reading Latin letters with an Arabic voice
• Faster startup: a Baseline Profile now ships for the critical paths (settings activity, voice-selection screen, speech and announcement services) so the hot path is compiled and merged at install time — the app launches quicker; your later install stays safe too (note: it profiles only dependencies, never replaces your profile)
• Arabic tashkeel can now be preserved: a new "keep diacritics" switch in the screen-reader settings hands your words back to the app with their original vowel marks instead of stripping them — for those who want the text spoken exactly as written
• Engine discovery is invalidated the moment packages change on the system: installing, removing or updating a TTS engine (including external engines like MultiTTS) makes its languages and voices available in the app immediately — no waiting for the freshness window to expire
• Settings stay fresh across processes, safely: a direct change notification (ContentObserver) refreshes the settings the moment another copy edits them (instead of clock comparisons), and that refresh reads without writing at all — no write races, no stale announcements after an edit
• Smoother, more even voice across engines: a dynamic RMS loudness gain pulls every engine toward the same target so mixed-engine speech no longer jumps between quiet and loud; a short crossfade blends the chunk borders so hard clicks disappear; synthesis sessions scale with the engines actually installed (no fixed cap); and the stream deadline extends on every successfully emitted chunk so a slow-but-still-writing engine is never cut off
• English as a complete second language for text conversion: numbers, currencies, dates, phone numbers, symbols and punctuation are now spoken in correct English whenever the announced text is English (Arabic stays unchanged), and URLs are masked from punctuation so they are never mangled
• Cleaner service shutdown: the background warm-up job is cancelled and the interruption-sensor monitor is stopped the moment the service is destroyed, so no resources stay pinned
• More reliable speech start: the warm-up job is prepared lazily and started only after the request handle is pinned, so it never competes with an incoming speech request
• TalkBack speech is now stable against engine races: the request path no longer relies on two shared engine fields (instance/engine) — the engine pool is the single source of truth, so speech can never ride an abandoned instance or a stale engine; byte-pool ownership is now strict (the provider never returns its own source, only the pooled scaled result) which eliminates the double-release hazard in mixed-stream merging; and the success flag is atomic so a channel can never be closed twice
• Faster, cleaner engine startup: language discovery and navigation-word PCM warm-up are merged into one background task that is cancelled the moment a real speech request arrives; discovery is guarded by a one-at-a-time lock; and the journey handle is assigned before execution so stop commands are honored instantly even at launch
• Root-cause fix for the lone English word: the synthesis language now follows the actual unit language (languageTag) instead of the request language, so an English word is never spoken with the Arabic voice even when the UI language is Arabic (items 17/18)
• Stable engine voice with no mid-sentence switch: an engine instance is published to the pool and made active only after its onInit succeeds — any parallel unit arriving mid-init waits for it to mature instead of grabbing an uninitialized instance and bouncing to another engine with a different voice (races item)
• The audio cache is no longer flushed on engine/language switch: cache keys already carry the engine, so each engine's entries stay warm across switches and repeated phrases are served instantly from memory — a real gain for mixed-language speech (item 19.1)
• More precise settings freshness across the two processes: the settings file length is now watched alongside its timestamp, so a second write within the same second is picked up and applied immediately instead of waiting for a restart (races item)
• Fixed the voice of a lone English word in app announcements: it is now spoken with a real English voice (the engine voice is picked explicitly by the unit's language) instead of falling on the Arabic voice even though it stayed an independent unit (item 18)
• Code cleanup: removed a redundant null check and a compiler warning in the speech-unit merge (item 18) — no change in audible behavior
• Removed multiple silences in multi-choice announcements (checked/unchecked): consecutive segments on the same voice are now merged into one continuous utterance regardless of rate/pitch/volume differences (item 18)
• A lone English word (app name / proper noun) stays as an independent unit spoken with the English voice and is no longer merged into Arabic segments on the Arabic voice (item 18)
• Root-fix for mixed-language announcements: Arabic and English words inside one sentence are now spoken as a single continuous utterance with no ~1-second silence between them (the new merge unifies consecutive segments on the same system voice even when their languages differ), while per-language custom voices stay fully separate as before (item 17)

• Faster, smoother announcements: consecutive identical speech segments are merged into one seamless unit with no choppy break between them, and the two cue-to-speech gaps are cut from 150 to 80 ms and from 250 to 120 ms — voice starts with no audible silence or harsh click between parts
• SMS, caller and battery announcement receivers now hold a short transient partial WakeLock (6 seconds = the broadcast window, self-releasing via acquire-timeout — the unified TimeAlarmReceiver pattern) so the device never sleeps mid-speech; announcement speech and its cues (clock/alarm tones) are pinned to SPATIALIZATION_BEHAVIOR_NEVER on Android 13+ so the track stays front and center with no spatial scattering; and the time alarm is rebuilt immediately when the exact-alarm permission is granted or revoked
• Shake/proximity interruption sensors are now wired into the screen-reader speech path (NateqTtsService): screen reading halts instantly on shake or proximity, just like in-app announcements
• Continuous common phase (16.16) across successive chunks in [PcmResampler]: consecutive chunks on the same slice share a single phase (LongArray(2)) and resume where they stopped — no restart from zero at chunk boundaries, removing the audible clicks at chunk transitions
• Correct thousands phrasing for 101 and 102: «مائة ألف وألف» and «مائة ألف وألفان» instead of «مائة وواحد ألف» (and the same fix applies to millions and billions)
• Defensive hardening: explicit invalidation of stale utterance IDs on every FLUSH/stop cycle, a safe speech-rate ceiling to prevent Samsung engine hangs above 2.5, and a unified battery-sticky reader shared between the health screen and the time-announcement scheduler
• Speech quality round 1–6: «الساعة 5 م» reads as a time (not meters), «0,125» is a decimal fraction (not thousands), lowercase Roman numerals such as «الفصل iii» are spoken, negative amounts like «ناقص دولاران» are phrased correctly, Long values survive backups intact, and <string-set> text groups are read across processes
• Two new settings: a dedicated pitch bar for caller, SMS and battery announcements, and an "always on the media stream" switch for announcements
• Clock widget: click broadcasts are guarded by a private token and a closed (non-exported) receiver — no speech from outside apps
• SMS reading: in "source only" mode the source is spoken even when a custom template exists
• v19 stability fix: an unescaped apostrophe in the English changelog had broken resource compilation (v18 shipped clean of it)
• v18 audit round: the unknown caller number is spoken digit by digit, the announcement pitch (caller/SMS/battery/widget) follows the speech settings instead of fixed 1.0, the SMS/notification engine override is honored, the battery falls back to the chosen language voice, time cues use the correct day part (00:xx = after midnight), the مائتا billion phrasing is fixed, negative fraction amounts keep their sign, multi-process prefs handling is safer, and more language codes are mapped
• Full audit sweep (Sections 1–4): more reliable time, caller, SMS and battery announcements and cleaner number/text speech
• TalkBack accessibility: the language tools and custom-name delete buttons identify their target by name, and opening a section is read through headings
• UI stability: the settings screen keeps its position across rotation, every section clears its view references (no memory leaks), and the preview engine closes immediately
• Clock widget: the disabled text matches the speech voice language, and the widget refreshes as soon as the app language changes
• Quick Settings tile: turning announcements off now cancels the time alarms for good (no battery-draining background wake-ups)
• Section summaries refresh instantly when the number-speech mode changes or SMS permission is granted
• Removed an unused layout file and slimmed the app size
• Device compatibility guidance (Axis 3): vendor-aware help for Xiaomi/Huawei/Oppo/Vivo/Samsung with buttons that open the right battery and autostart screens
• Flexible engine fallback chain: peripheral engines (MultiTTS/eSpeak) first, then native, then alphabetical — Google is the last resort
• Alert when your chosen engine fails and speech switches to another engine
• "Make the default engine" button in the first-run setup, with auto-convert enabled automatically when an engine is chosen
• Speech completion watchdog: audio focus is released automatically if any engine hangs (no stuck focus)
• Safe import defaults: shake/proximity and smart spelling are reset on restore
• Temporary voice cache cleanup when the active engine switches
• Greater stability for hourly chime, time and message announcements and battery cues through comprehensive automated tests
• Correct "quarter to" phrasing: 11:45 is said as midday (ظهراً), not morning
• Time announcements survive app updates (alarms are re-scheduled automatically)
• Security: the APK checksum is verified from the release notes before installing
• "Reset to defaults" now clears the pronunciation dictionary from memory and disk
• Fixed hundreds and thousands pronunciation (مائة، ألف، ثمانون…) after the number engine rework
• Audio slider changes stay saved while using the TalkBack screen reader
• Slider rate and pitch values are read with proper localized digits (١٫٥×) instead of a literal TalkBack reading
• Unified notification buttons: "Announce now" and "Stop"
• A natural spoken phrase when returning to the main list
• Fixed the "app keeps stopping" (ANR) in caller/SMS/battery/time announcements — pending broadcasts now finish immediately, with a safe cap well below the system timeout
• The settings chevrons are proper vector icons (RTL-aware) instead of text glyphs
• The speaking clock widget can be resized (with a larger default size) and the service notification is categorized and visible on the lock screen
• Clean speech for keycap emoji (1️⃣) and tag-based flags in notification emoji
• Improved architecture: the settings store now sits behind scoped contracts for speech, announcements, conversion and privacy, with one unified instance via Hilt and a single shared factory
• Raised the temporary speech cache ceiling on powerful devices (4 MB) for longer cached phrases
• Speech starts while the alert cue plays — no dead air after the beep
• Auto-detection of the Latin script language in mixed text (English/French/German/Spanish)
• Boot warm-up: installed TTS engines are pre-bound and common navigation words play straight from a pre-warmed cache
• Mixed speech (Arabic + Latin) synthesizes in parallel: segments of different languages are produced together and streamed in order — faster short phrases
• Common acronyms are spelled out by their resulting letters instead of being read as text («إلخ» → ت.إ.ت)
• Chunked synthesis streaming: long texts begin speaking early — no waiting for the full file
